## OBO — Item 1 of 15

### [#54 Error Analyzing Job in session with job present](https://github.com/Warnes-Innovations/cv-builder/issues/54) — BUG

**Classification:** Actionable bug
**Evidence:**
- **Reset puts UI in wrong state** — after Reset, the job-descriptor tabs appear instead of showing the already-loaded job. This is a workflow-state regression in the session restore path.
- **Confirm job details shown pre-analysis** — the prompt to confirm job title/company fires before the LLM analyzes the job posting, reversing the intended order (analyze → extract → confirm).
- **Confirm and Analyze produces additional errors** — even if the user fills in the form manually, the flow fails, suggesting a backend error in the analyze-job route with a pre-populated session.

**Likely areas:** `job_routes.py` (or equivalent analyze-job handler), `conversation_manager.py` phase transitions, UI session-state restoration logic in `src`.

**Suggested next action:** Switch to implementation mode and reproduce/fix the Reset→Analyze flow sequencing.

Now also look at where  and  end up:  I have everything needed. Here's the full elaboration:

---

## The Two Intake-Confirmation Code Paths

There are two separate mechanisms that show the "Confirm job details" form. They are architecturally different and designed for different moments in the workflow:

---

### Path A —  → intake card *after* analysis (the **fixed** path)

**Trigger:** User clicks **🔍 Analyze Job** button (or the session auto-analyzes on reload).

**Sequence:**
```
[Analyze Job btn]
  → POST /api/action  { action: 'analyze_job' }
  ← LLM runs, returns analysis, title, company, questions
  ← display analysis text + formatted analysis panel
  ← switch to 'analysis' tab
  → GET /api/intake-metadata
       ├─ if confirmed==true  →  _proceedAfterIntake()  →  askPostAnalysisQuestions()
       └─ if confirmed==false →  _showIntakeConfirmCard()  [chat-appended mini-card]
                                    ├─ "Confirm & Continue"  →  POST /api/confirm-intake  →  _proceedAfterIntake()
                                    └─ "Skip"               →  _proceedAfterIntake()
```

The intake card in this path is **a small card appended to the chat thread, inside the analysis tab** — implemented by  in `message-dispatch.js`. It fires **after** the LLM has already parsed the job, so the Role and Company fields are pre-filled with values the LLM extracted (the `status_routes.py` fix in `af7cb29` ensures this). The user confirms or corrects them, and the flow continues to post-analysis clarifying questions. This is the correct ordering and is the design intent.

---

### Path B —  /  /  → full-page form *before* analysis

**Trigger:** User pastes text and clicks **Submit Job Description**, or fetches from URL, or uploads a file.

**Sequence (all three entry points funnel the same way):**
```
[Submit / Fetch URL / Upload File]
  → POST /api/job  { job_text: ... }          ← stores job in session state
  ← "✅ Job description submitted successfully."
  → showIntakeConfirmation()                   ← full-page form replaces document-content
       ├─ GET /api/intake-metadata             ← heuristic only (no job_analysis yet)
       ├─ GET /api/prior-clarifications
       └─ renders full form in #document-content
            ├─ "Confirm & Start Analysis"  →  confirmIntakeAndAnalyze()
            │                                   → POST /api/confirm-intake
            │                                   → analyzeJob()   ← NOW the LLM runs
            └─ "Skip"  →  skipIntakeConfirmation()  → analyzeJob()
```

This form is **a full-page replacement** of the document viewer, implemented by  in `job-input.js`. It fires **before** analysis runs. That is **intentional**: the job text was just submitted raw, the LLM has not yet parsed it, so the server can only use regex/heuristics to pre-fill Role and Company from the first two lines of the text. The user can correct those guesses before the LLM wastes a slow API call on a mislabelled session directory name. Analysis only fires after they click "Confirm & Start Analysis".

The reason the pre-fill here is weaker than in Path A is structural — no job_analysis exists yet at this point. The `status_routes.py` fix improves Path A's pre-fill; it has no effect on Path B because the LLM hasn't run yet when Path B's form is shown.

---

### Why this matters for issue #54

The bug in #54 was triggered via Path A: the user loaded an *existing session* (which already had a job and prior ), then pressed the **Analyze Job** button. In that scenario,  should already be `True` (the prior session had it confirmed), so  should skip. The pre-fix code showed the card anyway because it was calling heuristic extraction instead of reading  — and when the user filled it in and clicked Confirm,  inside Path A then crashed due to the  bug.

Path B is unrelated to #54 and is correct by design — "confirm before you analyze" is the right UX when the job has *just* been pasted.

---

import esbuild from 'esbuild';
import { resolve, dirname } from 'path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'url';

const __dirname = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
const root = resolve(__dirname, '..');

const args      = new Set(process.argv.slice(2));
const isProd    = args.has('--prod');
const isWatch   = args.has('--watch');
const sourcemap = args.has('--sourcemap') || !isProd;

/** @type {import('esbuild').BuildOptions} */
const config = {
  entryPoints: [resolve(root, 'web/src/main.js')],
  bundle:      true,
  outfile:     resolve(root, 'web/bundle.js'),
  format:      'iife',   // wraps in (function(){ … })() — safe for <script> tags
  target:      ['es2020'],
  minify:      isProd,
  sourcemap:   sourcemap ? 'inline' : false,
  banner: {
    js: '/* cv-builder bundle — built by esbuild, do not edit directly */',
  },
};

if (isWatch) {
  const ctx = await esbuild.context(config);
  await ctx.watch();
  const kb = '(watching)';
  console.log(`⏳ esbuild watching web/src/main.js → web/bundle.js`);
} else {
  const result = await esbuild.build({ ...config, metafile: true });
  const kb = (
    Object.values(result.metafile.outputs)[0].bytes / 1024
  ).toFixed(1);
  console.log(`✓ web/bundle.js  ${kb} KB${isProd ? '  (minified)' : ''}`);
}
```

**Description:** Audit overlap between auto-analyze on init and manual Analyze button path in `web/app.js` — confirm no race/double-call regressions under session-restore timing edge cases. 

Now I have the full picture. Let me assess:

**Auto-analyze path** (`init()`, line ~55):
```
if (!stateManager.isReconnecting()) {
    const status = await fetchStatus();
    if (!status._error && status.job_description && !status.job_analysis) {
        await analyzeJob();
    }
}
```

**Manual analyze path** (`analyze-btn` click → `analyzeJob()`):
```js
if (stateManager.isLoading()) return;   // guard at top of analyzeJob()
```

**Assessment:** The two paths are already correctly protected:

1. **Auto-analyze only fires when `job_analysis` is absent** — checked via `fetchStatus()` before calling. If the user has already analyzed, the `else if (status.job_analysis)` branch logs and skips.
2. **The guard `if (stateManager.isLoading()) return`** at the top of `analyzeJob()` prevents any double-call while analysis is in flight — whether it was started by auto-analyze or the button.
3. **`_listenersRegistered` flag** ensures `setupEventListeners()` is idempotent — the button listener is never registered twice.
4. **`stateManager.isReconnecting()`** short-circuits the entire auto-analyze block on session restore, preventing a redundant re-analysis of an already-analyzed session.

No race condition is possible: `init()` is `async` and sequentially `await`s `restoreSession()` → `fetchStatus()` → `analyzeJob()`. **Description:** Audit overlap between auto-analyze on init and manual Analyze button path in `app.js` — confirm no race/double-call regressions under session-restore timing edge cases. Now I have the full picture. Let me assess:

**Auto-analyze path** (`init()`, line ~55):
```
if (!stateManager.isReconnecting()) {

**Manual analyze path** (`analyze-btn` click → `analyzeJob()`):
```js

**Assessment:** The two paths are already correctly protected:

1. **Auto-analyze only fires when `job_analysis` is absent** — checked via `fetchStatus()` before calling. If the user has already analyzed, the `else if (status.job_analysis)` branch logs and skips.
2. **The guard `if (stateManager.isLoading()) return`** at the top of `analyzeJob()` prevents any double-call while analysis is in flight — whether it was started by auto-analyze or the button.
3. **`_listenersRegistered` flag** ensures `setupEventListeners()` is idempotent — the button listener is never registered twice.
4. **`stateManager.isReconnecting()`** short-circuits the entire auto-analyze block on session restore, preventing a redundant re-analysis of an already-analyzed session.

No race condition is possible: `init()` is `async` and sequentially `await`s `restoreSession()` → `fetchStatus()` → `analyzeJob()`. The button handler can't fire before `setupEventListeners()` runs, which is called on the same microtask line as `analyzeJob()` being awaited — but by then `isLoading()` would be `true` anyway.

**Finding: No action needed. The idempotency is correctly implemented through three complementary guards.**  **Item 3 result: No code changes needed.** Three guards work in concert:

| Guard | Where | What it prevents |
|---|---|---|
| `status.job_analysis` check | `init()` auto-analyze block | Re-analyzing an already-analyzed session |
| `stateManager.isReconnecting()` | `init()` auto-analyze block | Triggering analysis on session reconnect |
| `stateManager.isLoading()` | top of `analyzeJob()` | Concurrent calls from button while analysis is running |

_**Agent (copilot/auto)**_

Item 4 is the architectural boundary check: should /api/message and /api/action stay separate, or be unified.  
The short answer is yes, they should stay separate, and here is why in concrete terms.

**What each endpoint means**
1. /api/message is conversational input.
2. /api/action is structured workflow control.

That boundary is visible in backend routing:
1. Message route: [scripts/routes/job_routes.py](scripts/routes/job_routes.py#L426)
2. Action route: [scripts/routes/job_routes.py](scripts/routes/job_routes.py#L468)

**Different backend execution paths**
1. /api/message calls conversation._process_message(msg), which:
   1. Appends user/assistant history.
   2. Builds system prompt + history.
   3. Lets the LLM drive next behavior.
   4. Optionally parses embedded action requests from assistant output.
   5. Saves conversational state.
   Reference: [scripts/utils/conversation_manager.py](scripts/utils/conversation_manager.py#L240)
2. /api/action calls conversation._execute_action(payload), which:
   1. Executes known action types directly.
   2. Performs deterministic phase/workflow transitions.
   3. Returns structured results for UI orchestration.
   Reference: [scripts/utils/conversation_manager.py](scripts/utils/conversation_manager.py#L494)

**Different API contracts**
1. /api/message returns MessageResponse with response.
2. /api/action returns ActionResponse with result.
References:
1. [scripts/web_app.py](scripts/web_app.py#L179)
2. [scripts/web_app.py](scripts/web_app.py#L188)

Even though frontend validation currently uses one parser for both, that does not mean semantics are the same:
1. Parser: [web/validators.js](web/validators.js#L74)

**Frontend usage is also intentionally split**
1. Chat flows post to /api/message:
   1. [web/message-dispatch.js](web/message-dispatch.js#L42)
2. Deterministic workflow actions post to /api/action:
   1. [web/job-analysis.js](web/job-analysis.js#L102)
   2. [web/session-actions.js](web/session-actions.js#L51)

**Why this split is valuable**
1. It keeps conversational ambiguity away from deterministic workflow controls.
2. It keeps intent explicit in logs, tests, and error handling.
3. It reduces accidental regressions where chat text could trigger workflow mutations unexpectedly.
4. It allows different response shaping without overloading one endpoint.

**What would go wrong if merged**
1. Endpoint semantics would blur, making client behavior harder to reason about.
2. Retry/loading/progress handling would likely diverge again because “message” and “action” UX lifecycles are not identical.
3. Conversation history side-effects could leak into flows that should be transactional.

**Conclusion**
Item 4 was classified correctly as intentional architecture, not redundant duplication.  
No code change was needed.  

If you want, I can do one follow-up hardening pass: add a short contract comment near both route handlers in [scripts/routes/job_routes.py](scripts/routes/job_routes.py#L426) and [scripts/routes/job_routes.py](scripts/routes/job_routes.py#L468) so this boundary is explicit for future contributors.

import json
from pathlib import Path

try:
    from pypdf import PdfReader
except Exception:
    PdfReader = None


def load_runs(path: Path):
    data = json.loads(path.read_text())
    if "profiles" in data:
        for profile_name, profile in data["profiles"].items():
            for idx, run in enumerate(profile.get("raw_runs", []), start=1):
                yield profile_name, idx, run
    else:
        for idx, run in enumerate(data.get("raw_runs", []), start=1):
            yield data.get("profile", "unknown"), idx, run


def html_signals(html_text: str):
    lower = html_text.lower()
    empty_section_markers = 0
    candidates = [
        "<div class=\"section\"></div>",
        "<section></section>",
        "<ul></ul>",
        "<ol></ol>",
    ]
    for c in candidates:
        empty_section_markers += lower.count(c)

    headings = lower.count('class="section-title"') + lower.count("class='section-title'")
    items = (
        lower.count('class="experience-item"')
        + lower.count('class="achievement-item"')
        + lower.count('class="pub-item"')
        + lower.count('<li')
    )
    return {
        "empty_markers": empty_section_markers,
        "section_titles": headings,
        "content_items": items,
    }


def pdf_signals(pdf_path: Path):
    if PdfReader is None:
        return {"error": "pypdf unavailable"}
    reader = PdfReader(str(pdf_path))
    lengths = []
    for page in reader.pages:
        text = page.extract_text() or ""
        lengths.append(len(text.strip()))
    near_blank_pages = [i + 1 for i, n in enumerate(lengths) if n < 80]
    return {
        "pages": len(lengths),
        "text_lengths": lengths,
        "near_blank_pages": near_blank_pages,
    }


def main():
    src = Path("/tmp/issue61_compare_sweep.json")
    if not src.exists():
        raise SystemExit("missing /tmp/issue61_compare_sweep.json")

    findings = []
    for profile, idx, run in load_runs(src):
        paths = run.get("paths", {})
        html_path = Path(paths.get("html", ""))
        pdf_path = Path(paths.get("pdf", ""))
        row = {
            "profile": profile,
            "run": idx,
            "status": run.get("status"),
            "html": str(html_path),
            "pdf": str(pdf_path),
        }

        if html_path.exists():
            row["html_signals"] = html_signals(html_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"))
        else:
            row["html_signals"] = {"error": "missing html"}

        if pdf_path.exists():
            row["pdf_signals"] = pdf_signals(pdf_path)
        else:
            row["pdf_signals"] = {"error": "missing pdf"}

        findings.append(row)

    print(json.dumps(findings, indent=2))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

- content:

```
import json
import re
from pathlib import Path
from pypdf import PdfReader

HEADINGS = [
    "PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE",
    "KEY ACHIEVEMENTS",
    "EDUCATION",
    "SKILLS",
    "PUBLICATIONS",
    "AWARDS",
    "SUMMARY",
]


def load_runs(path: Path):
    data = json.loads(path.read_text())
    for profile, block in data.get("profiles", {}).items():
        for idx, run in enumerate(block.get("raw_runs", []), start=1):
            yield profile, idx, run


def norm_lines(text: str):
    lines = [re.sub(r"\s+", " ", ln).strip() for ln in text.splitlines()]
    return [ln for ln in lines if ln]


def check_pdf(pdf_path: Path):
    r = PdfReader(str(pdf_path))
    page_findings = []
    for i, p in enumerate(r.pages, start=1):
        lines = norm_lines(p.extract_text() or "")
        tail = lines[-5:] if len(lines) >= 5 else lines
        tail_up = [t.upper() for t in tail]
        orphan_heading = any(any(h in t for h in HEADINGS) for t in tail_up)
        page_findings.append({
            "page": i,
            "tail": tail,
            "possible_orphan_heading_at_page_end": orphan_heading,
        })
    return page_findings


src = Path("/tmp/issue61_compare_sweep.json")
rows = []
for profile, idx, run in load_runs(src):
    pdf = Path(run.get("paths", {}).get("pdf", ""))
    if not pdf.exists():
        continue
    pf = check_pdf(pdf)
    suspicious = [x for x in pf if x["possible_orphan_heading_at_page_end"]]
    rows.append({
        "profile": profile,
        "run": idx,
        "pages": len(pf),
        "suspicious_pages": suspicious,
    })

print(json.dumps(rows, indent=2))

```

<tool-use data-tool-type="write" data-tool-name="create_file"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **create_file**</summary>

**Input:**

- content:

```
import json
import re
from pathlib import Path
from pypdf import PdfReader

HEADINGS = [
    "PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE",
    "KEY ACHIEVEMENTS",
    "EDUCATION",
    "SKILLS",
    "PUBLICATIONS",
    "SELECTED PUBLICATIONS",
    "AWARDS",
    "SUMMARY",
]


def load_runs(path: Path):
    data = json.loads(path.read_text())
    for profile, block in data.get("profiles", {}).items():
        for idx, run in enumerate(block.get("raw_runs", []), start=1):
            yield profile, idx, run


def norm_lines(text: str):
    lines = [re.sub(r"\s+", " ", ln).strip() for ln in text.splitlines()]
    return [ln for ln in lines if ln]


def check_pdf(pdf_path: Path):
    r = PdfReader(str(pdf_path))
    page_findings = []
    for i, p in enumerate(r.pages, start=1):
        lines = norm_lines(p.extract_text() or "")
        tail = lines[-5:] if len(lines) >= 5 else lines
        tail_up = [t.upper() for t in tail]
        orphan_heading = any(any(h in t for h in HEADINGS) for t in tail_up)
        page_findings.append({
            "page": i,
            "tail": tail,
            "possible_orphan_heading_at_page_end": orphan_heading,
        })
    return page_findings


src = Path("/tmp/issue61_compare_sweep_postfix.json")
rows = []
for profile, idx, run in load_runs(src):
    pdf = Path(run.get("paths", {}).get("pdf", ""))
    if not pdf.exists():
        continue
    pf = check_pdf(pdf)
    suspicious = [x for x in pf if x["possible_orphan_heading_at_page_end"]]
    rows.append({
        "profile": profile,
        "run": idx,
        "pages": len(pf),
        "suspicious_pages": suspicious,
    })

print(json.dumps(rows, indent=2))

```

- filePath: `/tmp/issue61_orphan_check_postfix.py`

_**User (2026-03-31 23:25:41Z)**_

Is there any reason to preserve any more than the latest HTML/PDF preview artifacts?

---

_**Agent (copilot/auto)**_

Short answer: yes, but only a little.

Keeping only the single latest preview set is usually fine for normal user flow, but a small buffer can still be useful for:

1. In-flight request overlap
1. If two preview/refine requests are close together, preserving one or two prior sets avoids broken links while UI state catches up.

2. Debug and support diagnostics
1. A recent prior artifact helps compare “before vs after” when diagnosing layout regressions or renderer differences.

3. Renderer fallback resilience
1. If one renderer output is bad or missing for the newest request, a very recent prior set gives a safe fallback for quick inspection.

So the practical policy is:
1. Keep latest only if disk pressure is critical and you accept less diagnosability.
2. Keep a small fixed window (for example 3 to 6 request groups) for better robustness with minimal storage cost.

Given your current flow, keeping only latest is possible, but keeping a small window is the safer default with little downside.

/**
 * web/ats-refinement.js
 * ATS score badge display and debounced refresh scheduling.
 *
 * DEPENDENCIES:
 *   - stateManager from state-manager.js (on globalThis)
 */

function updateAtsBadge(score) {
  const badge   = document.getElementById('ats-score-badge');
  const valueEl = document.getElementById('ats-score-value');
  if (!badge || !valueEl) return;

  if (!score || typeof score.overall !== 'number') {
    badge.style.display = 'none';
    return;
  }

  const overall = Math.round(score.overall);
  valueEl.textContent = `${overall}%`;
  badge.style.display = 'flex';

  badge.classList.remove('score-high', 'score-medium', 'score-low');
  if (overall >= 75) {
    badge.classList.add('score-high');
  } else if (overall >= 50) {
    badge.classList.add('score-medium');
  } else {
    badge.classList.add('score-low');
  }

  badge.setAttribute('aria-label', `ATS match score: ${overall}% (${score.basis || 'review'})`);
}

#62 is GitHub issue 62 in cv-builder:

Persist render-ready content for deterministic layout preview, estimate, and restore  
https://github.com/Warnes-Innovations/cv-builder/issues/62

In short, it asks to store a single render-ready snapshot in session state after customization decisions, then reuse that same snapshot for:
1. layout preview
2. layout estimate
3. restored preview after reload
4. final generation

The goal is to remove live-LLM dependency and nondeterminism in those later stages, so preview/estimate/final all run from the same persisted content basis.

<summary>Tool use: **mcp_gitkraken_pull_request_create**</summary>

**Input:**

- body:

```
## Summary

Implements issue #62: persistent render snapshots that enable deterministic layout previews and estimates after customization, with async throttled regeneration on content changes.

## Changes

- **Render snapshot persistence**: Added SHA256 signature-based caching of the final preview HTML after job analysis + customizations. Signature is computed from job analysis, materialized customizations, approved rewrites, spell audit, and max_skills.

- **Async throttled refresh**: On submit-time content/layout mutations (review decisions, achievements, skills, rewrites, spell-check, layout settings), a debounced async refresh is scheduled (1.5s debounce interval, per-session lock to prevent concurrent refreshes).

- **Layout-estimate optimization**: When no override payload is present, `/api/cv/layout-estimate` now reuses the persisted snapshot HTML instead of re-materializing, reducing determinism variance.

- **Generation-state metadata**: Exposed snapshot status fields (`render_snapshot_generated_at`, `render_snapshot_stale`, `render_snapshot_regenerating`) in `/api/cv/generation-state` for client-side tracking and restore capability.

## Testing

- `tests/test_staged_generation.py`: Updated schema assertions for new snapshot metadata fields.
- Targeted regressions: 43 passed in staged-generation tests; focused review-route and staged-generation subsets passed.

## Determinism Strategy

- Preview and layout-estimate paths now prefer the persisted snapshot when available, or fall back to deterministic materialization (`use_semantic_match=False`).
- Snapshot signature validation ensures staleness detection and regeneration triggers.
- No changes to Master CV during customization (snapshot persists in session state only per critical workflow windows).
```

I'll create a comprehensive end-to-end implementation plan for #75. Let me map out the architecture, decisions, and tasks:

## **Issue #75 Implementation Plan: Settings UI**

### **Current State**
- Config system in place: `config.yaml` + `.env` + environment variables with strict precedence
- Config validation via `ConfigValidator` in `config.py`
- No user-facing Settings UI; users edit config files directly
- Web app already loads config via `get_config()` at startup

### **Key Decisions**

| Decision | Choice | Rationale |
|----------|--------|-----------|
| Where to persist settings? | `config.yaml` writes + session state overrides | Respect precedence; session settings allow temporary user overrides without file edits |
| How to expose effective config? | New `/api/settings` endpoint (GET/PUT) | Non-intrusive; mirrors existing API pattern |
| Show precedence warnings in UI? | Yes, badge/tag for "env override" | Users understand why changes don't persist |
| Session-specific vs global? | Both: global settings (config.yaml) + session temp overrides | Flexibility for per-job customization |
| What settings to expose? | All configurable options from issue description | Sufficient for MVP; can expand later |

### **Architecture**

**Backend:**
- New `scripts/routes/settings_routes.py` with `create_blueprint(deps)` pattern
- `GET /api/settings` — read effective config (merged precedence + UI metadata)
- `PUT /api/settings` — update `config.yaml` with validation
- Helper to track precedence source (env vs .env vs `config.yaml`)

**Frontend:**
- New `web/src/components/SettingsPanel.js` — modal/drawer with form controls
- Integrate into app navigation (settings icon/button in header)
- Real-time validation feedback, save confirmation
- Display precedence warnings (e.g., "Overridden by environment variable CV_LLM_PROVIDER")

**Data Flow:**
```
SettingsPanel (form) 
  → PUT /api/settings {field, value}
    → validate & merge with existing config.yaml
    → write to disk
    → return effective config + source info
  → update UI (show success, precedence tags)
```

**Session Integration:**
- Option to save settings as session temp (UI toggle: "Just this session")
- Session overrides picked up in `ConversationManager` config resolution

### **Risk & Mitigation**

| Risk | Mitigation |
|------|-----------|
| Writing to `config.yaml` breaks other sessions | Atomic file ops; test concurrent writes; read-back validation |
| Precedence UX confusion | Show source badge for each setting (🔒 env, 📄 config.yaml, ⚙️ default) |
| Invalid config crashes app | Client-side validation + server-side schema validation before write |
| Session-specific conflicts | Separate session override map; apply at resolution time |

### **Task Breakdown**

**Phase 1: Backend Infrastructure** (3 tasks)
1. Create `settings_routes.py` with GET/PUT endpoints + validation
2. Add `_get_effective_config()` helper with precedence source tracking
3. Add unit tests for endpoints (read, write, validation, precedence)

**Phase 2: Frontend Component** (3 tasks)
4. Create `SettingsPanel.js` with form controls (timeout, provider, model, generation defaults, format toggles)
5. Add SettingsPanel integration into main app layout (nav icon → modal trigger)
6. Add client-side validation and error handling

**Phase 3: Session Integration & Polish** (2 tasks)
7. Wire session temp-override toggle + storage
8. End-to-end testing: settings → config file → app behavior verification

**Phase 4: Review & Commit** (1 task)
9. Code review, test coverage check, commit with message

---

### **Success Criteria**
- [x] Settings endpoint reads effective config with precedence source metadata
- [x] Settings endpoint writes to `config.yaml` with validation + rollback
- [x] UI panel displays all configurable options with proper feedback
- [x] Precedence warnings shown ("Overridden by environment variable")
- [x] Tests pass (unit + integration + e2e)
- [x] Config precedence respected and unchanged

**Estimated effort:** 4–5 hours (backend ~2h, UI ~1.5h, integration ~1h, testing ~0.5h)  
**Complexity:** Medium (new feature + file I/O + precedence logic)

---

```
## Summary

Implements issue #75 end-to-end with a centralized Settings UI and safe backend settings API while preserving config precedence.

## What changed

- Added `GET /api/settings` and `PUT /api/settings` in `scripts/routes/status_routes.py`
  - Read effective settings with explicit source metadata per field (`env`, `.env`, `config`, `default`)
  - Validate incoming updates
  - Persist updates to `config.yaml` via guarded, atomic write flow

- Added settings client API helpers in `web/api-client.js`
  - `fetchSettings()`
  - `updateSettings(settings)`

- Added a new header Settings entry point and modal in `web/index.html`
  - LLM defaults: provider/model/timeout/temperature
  - Generation defaults: max skills/achievements/publications, skills section title, format toggles
  - Save/reload actions and source labels

- Added settings modal behavior in `web/ui-core.js`
  - Load settings on open
  - Render values + source/locked hints
  - Submit updates and surface status feedback

- Added focused test coverage
  - Backend: `tests/test_api_integration.py::TestSettingsAPI`
  - Frontend: `tests/js/ui-core.test.js` settings modal tests

- Regenerated `web/bundle.js` and tracked implementation workflow in
  - `tasks/issue-75-settings-ui-plan.md`

## Verification

- `conda run -n cvgen python -m pytest tests/test_api_integration.py -k settings -q --tb=short`
  - `2 passed, 18 deselected`
- `npx vitest run tests/js/ui-core.test.js`
  - `6 passed`
- `npm run build`
  - Success (`web/bundle.js` regenerated)

## Notes

- Source precedence is preserved and surfaced to users:
  - `env vars > .env > config.yaml > defaults`
- Includes a follow-up fix from review to ensure metadata also reports env precedence correctly when both env and `.env` are present.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Systematic fix for all 23 exception exposure issues."""
import re

def fix_master_data_routes():
    """Fix 20 exposures in master_data_routes.py"""
    with open('/Users/warnes/src/cv-builder/scripts/routes/master_data_routes.py', 'r') as f:
        content = f.read()
    
    # Map of patterns to replace - each tuple is (find_pattern, replacement)
    fixes = [
        # Line 242 - achievement update
        (r'(return jsonify\({"ok": True, "action": action, "id": ach_id}\))\n        except Exception as e:\n            return jsonify\({"ok": False, "error": str\(e\)}\), 500',
         r'\1\n        except Exception as e:\n            logger.exception("Failed to update achievement")\n            return jsonify({"ok": False, "error": "Failed to update achievement"}), 500'),
        
        # Line 280 - summary update
        (r'(= text\n            master\[.professional_summaries.\] = summaries)\n            save_master\(master, master_path\)\n            return jsonify\({"ok": True, "action": "added" if is_new else "updated", "key": key}\)\n        except Exception as e:\n            return jsonify\({"ok": False, "error": str\(e\)}\), 500',
         r'\1\n            save_master(master, master_path)\n            return jsonify({"ok": True, "action": "added" if is_new else "updated", "key": key})\n        except Exception as e:\n            logger.exception("Failed to update summary")\n            return jsonify({"ok": False, "error": "Failed to update summary"}), 500'),
    ]
    
    for pattern, replacement in fixes:
        content = re.sub(pattern, replacement, content, flags=re.DOTALL)
    
    # Simpler approach: replace all str(e) in error messages with generic text
    # First collect all the error context from except blocks
    
    # Match the pattern: except Exception as (e|exc): ... return jsonify(..."error": str(e)...)
    # We'll do this line by line
    
    lines = content.split('\n')
    result_lines = []
    i = 0
    
    while i < len(lines):
        line = lines[i]
        
        # If we find an except Exception line followed later by a return with str(e)
        if 'except Exception as e:' in line or 'except Exception as exc:' in line:
            result_lines.append(line)
            i += 1
            
            # Look ahead for return jsonify lines with str(e) or str(exc)
            while i < len(lines) and ('return jsonify' not in lines[i] and 'except' not in lines[i]):
                result_lines.append(lines[i])
                i += 1
            
            # Now we should be at a return or another except
            if i < len(lines):
                if 'except' in lines[i]:
                    # Hit another except, continue
                    continue
                
                # Check if this return has str(e) or str(exc)
                if 'str(e)' in lines[i] or 'str(exc)' in lines[i]:
                    # Add logger call before the return
                    indent = len(lines[i]) - len(lines[i].lstrip())
                    result_lines.append(' ' * indent + 'logger.exception("Operation failed")')
                    # Now replace str(e) with generic message
                    # Determine appropriate message from context
                    if 'achievement' in '\n'.join(lines[max(0,i-20):i]):
                        msg = 'Failed to update achievement'
                    elif 'summary' in '\n'.join(lines[max(0,i-20):i]):
                        msg = 'Failed to update summary'
                    elif 'master-data' in '\n'.join(lines[max(0,i-20):i]) or 'full' in '\n'.join(lines[max(0,i-20):i]):
                        msg = 'Failed to load master data'
                    elif 'skill' in '\n'.join(lines[max(0,i-20):i]):
                        msg = 'Failed to update skill'
                    elif 'experience' in '\n'.join(lines[max(0,i-20):i]):
                        msg = 'Failed to update experience'
                    elif 'education' in '\n'.join(lines[max(0,i-20):i]):
                        msg = 'Failed to update education'
                    elif 'award' in '\n'.join(lines[max(0,i-20):i]):
                        msg = 'Failed to update award'
                    elif 'certification' in '\n'.join(lines[max(0,i-20):i]):
                        msg = 'Failed to update certification'
                    elif 'publication' in '\n'.join(lines[max(0,i-20):i]):
                        msg = 'Failed to update publication'
                    elif 'cover-letter' in '\n'.join(lines[max(0,i-20):i]):
                        msg = 'Failed with cover letter'
                    elif 'screening' in '\n'.join(lines[max(0,i-20):i]):
                        msg = 'Failed with screening'
                    else:
                        msg = 'Operation failed'
                    
                    # Replace str(e) or str(exc) in the return statement
                    line = lines[i]
                    line = line.replace('str(e)', f'"{msg}"')
                    line = line.replace('str(exc)', f'"{msg}"')
                    result_lines.append(line)
                    i += 1
                else:
                    result_lines.append(lines[i])
                    i += 1
        else:
            result_lines.append(line)
            i += 1
    
    content = '\n'.join(result_lines)
    
    with open('/Users/warnes/src/cv-builder/scripts/routes/master_data_routes.py', 'w') as f:
        f.write(content)
    
    print("Fixed master_data_routes.py")

def fix_session_routes():
    """Fix 1 exposure in session_routes.py"""
    with open('/Users/warnes/src/cv-builder/scripts/routes/session_routes.py', 'r') as f:
        content = f.read()
    
    # Replace the SessionOwnedError str(e) exposure
    content = content.replace(
        'return jsonify({"error": "session_owned", "message": str(e)}), 409',
        'logger.exception("Session ownership check failed")\n            return jsonify({"error": "session_owned", "message": "Session access denied"}), 409'
    )
    
    with open('/Users/warnes/src/cv-builder/scripts/routes/session_routes.py', 'w') as f:
        f.write(content)
    
    print("Fixed session_routes.py")

if __name__ == '__main__':
    fix_master_data_routes()
    fix_session_routes()
    print("All exception exposure fixes applied!")

_**User (2026-04-01 20:13:29Z)**_

Would it be better to add a new unit test that fails if the review discovers any issue, or to add a step to the PR github action to do this?

---

_**Agent (copilot/auto)**_

Better approach: add a dedicated PR GitHub Action step, not a regular unit test.

Why
1. The fixture review currently records environment-sensitive warnings in [tests/helpers/fixture_review.py](tests/helpers/fixture_review.py), such as missing Playwright Chromium. Turning that into a hard unit-test failure can create noisy local failures.
2. Unit tests in [tests/test_fixture_review.py](tests/test_fixture_review.py) should mostly validate structure and invariants (bundle exists, manifest shape, required artifacts).
3. Policy-style gating (fail PR if review flags issues) is CI behavior, so it belongs in workflow logic.

Best pattern
1. Keep existing unit tests as they are for correctness.
2. Add a strict check step in PR CI that runs the bundle generator and fails if manifest warnings/findings are non-empty.
3. Optionally support a strict mode flag in [scripts/generate_fixture_review_bundle.py](scripts/generate_fixture_review_bundle.py), then have CI call that mode.

This gives you stable local tests plus a clear merge gate in PRs. If you want, I can implement the CI gate now.

# Applicant Fixture Review

**Last Updated:** 2026-03-24 23:26 EDT

**Executive Summary:** The generated resume is readable but does not present itself as a polished final submission. The first page leaves a large dead zone beneath the summary, the sidebar dominates attention before the actual work history, and the repeated Technical Skills block makes the document feel unstable instead of intentional.

## Generated Materials Evaluation

- Finding 1: The first page spends too much space on summary and sidebar metadata while the core work history starts much lower on the page, which makes the resume feel unfinished. Evidence: `/tmp/issue59-phase3-bundle/normalized/render.png`, `/tmp/issue59-phase3-bundle/normalized/plain-text.txt`.
- Finding 2: The left rail is visually heavier than the main narrative because contact, education, awards, languages, and a large skills block all stack before the eye reaches experience. Evidence: `/tmp/issue59-phase3-bundle/normalized/render.png`.
- Finding 3: The repeated Technical Skills section near the end reads like a layout mistake rather than a deliberate continuation. Evidence: `/tmp/issue59-phase3-bundle/normalized/render.png`, `/tmp/issue59-phase3-bundle/normalized/structure-outline.txt`.

## Additional Story Gaps / Proposed Story Items

- Add a layout check that flags oversized first-page whitespace after summary/achievement sections.
- Add a duplicate-section detector for normalized review bundles.
```

_**Agent (copilot/auto)**_

Item 3 is:

1. Title: Add strict mode entrypoint for CI
2. Purpose: Make PR checks fail when fixture review reports review issues, instead of only recording warnings.

What “strict mode entrypoint” means
1. Add a flag to [scripts/generate_fixture_review_bundle.py](scripts/generate_fixture_review_bundle.py), for example `--strict`.
2. In strict mode, after bundle generation, inspect the manifest warnings/findings.
3. Exit non-zero if issues are present, so GitHub Actions marks the job failed.

Why this item exists
1. Current behavior is informational:
- [tests/helpers/fixture_review.py](tests/helpers/fixture_review.py) records warnings in the manifest/status files.
- [tests/test_fixture_review.py](tests/test_fixture_review.py) checks bundle integrity, not “zero findings.”
2. So today, review issues do not automatically block PR merge.
3. Item 3 adds the missing CI enforcement layer.

Practical implementation shape
1. Script layer:
- Update [scripts/generate_fixture_review_bundle.py](scripts/generate_fixture_review_bundle.py) with `--strict`.
- Read generated manifest and count blocking conditions (for example non-empty `warnings`, or a future `findings` section).
- `raise SystemExit(1)` on violations when strict is enabled.

2. Optional helper layer:
- Add a small helper in [tests/helpers/fixture_review.py](tests/helpers/fixture_review.py), e.g. `evaluate_fixture_review_manifest(manifest) -> list[str]`.
- Keep policy logic centralized and testable.

3. CI layer:
- Add a PR workflow step in `.github/workflows/*` that runs:
`conda run -n cvgen python scripts/generate_fixture_review_bundle.py --output-dir ... --strict`
- If strict fails, PR check fails.

Acceptance criteria for ID 3
1. Running strict mode with issue-free review exits `0`.
2. Running strict mode with warnings/findings exits non-zero.
3. CI invokes strict mode on PRs.
4. Clear console output explains exactly which findings triggered failure.

Non-goals
1. Do not convert all fixture-review unit tests into policy-gate tests.
2. Do not make local default run strict by default (to avoid disruptive local failures unless explicitly requested).

If you want, I can implement ID 3 now with:
1. `--strict` in the script,
2. one focused unit test for strict pass/fail behavior,
3. one PR workflow step to enforce it.

3. Policy enforcement (“block PR if review flags issues”) is better handled in CI workflow logic, not in the base unit test.

1. Keep tests reliable and deterministic.
2. Move merge-blocking policy to CI gates (item 3), where strict behavior is explicit and intentional.

Providing rationale/confidence helps users trust and edit recommendations for their specific context.","assignees":null}}

```
async function openCopilotAuthModal() {
  const statusRes = await fetch('/api/copilot-auth/status').then(r => r.json()).catch(() => ({}));
  if (statusRes.authenticated) {
    if (await confirmDialog('You are already authenticated with GitHub Copilot. Log out?', { confirmLabel: 'Log out', danger: true })) {
      await fetch('/api/copilot-auth/logout', { method: 'POST' });
      updateAuthBadge({ authenticated: false });
    }
    return;
  }

  const flowRes = await fetch('/api/copilot-auth/start', { method: 'POST' });
  if (!flowRes.ok) {
    alert('Failed to start auth flow: ' + (await flowRes.text()));
    return;
  }
  const flow = await flowRes.json();

  document.getElementById('auth-user-code').textContent   = flow.user_code;
  document.getElementById('auth-verify-link').href         = flow.verification_uri || 'https://github.com/login/device';
  document.getElementById('auth-verify-link').textContent  = flow.verification_uri || 'github.com/login/device';
  document.getElementById('auth-status-msg').textContent   = 'Waiting for you to enter the code at GitHub…';
  document.getElementById('auth-modal-overlay').classList.add('visible');
  if (typeof setInitialFocus === 'function') setInitialFocus('auth-modal-overlay');
  if (typeof trapFocus === 'function') trapFocus('auth-modal-overlay');

  await fetch('/api/copilot-auth/poll', { method: 'POST' });
  updateAuthBadge({ authenticated: false, polling: true });

  _authPollTimer = setInterval(async () => {
    const st = await fetch('/api/copilot-auth/status').then(r => r.json()).catch(() => ({}));
    updateAuthBadge(st);
    if (st.authenticated) {
      clearInterval(_authPollTimer);
      document.getElementById('auth-status-msg').textContent = '\u2713 Authenticated! Closing…';
      document.getElementById('auth-open-btn').disabled = true;
      setTimeout(closeCopilotAuthModal, 1200);
    } else if (st.error) {
      clearInterval(_authPollTimer);
      document.getElementById('auth-status-msg').textContent = '\u274C ' + st.error;
      updateAuthBadge({ authenticated: false });
    }
  }, 5000);
}

function openAuthGitHub() {
  const link = document.getElementById('auth-verify-link');
  window.open(link.href, '_blank');
}

function closeCopilotAuthModal() {
  document.getElementById('auth-modal-overlay').classList.remove('visible');
  if (_authPollTimer) { clearInterval(_authPollTimer); _authPollTimer = null; }
  if (typeof restoreFocus === 'function') restoreFocus();
}

Let me open your browser to the local instance: Excellent! The browser is open at `http://localhost:5002`. Now let's run through the LLM Configuration Wizard smoke test systematically. Here's the checklist for the wizard flow:

## Issue #81 LLM Configuration Wizard Smoke Test

### **Phase 1: App Load & Status Pill**
- [ ] Home page loads without errors
- [ ] Header shows LLM status pill (e.g., "GitHub / gemini-flash-latest" with a status icon)
- [ ] Pill color/styling matches design intent (blue for health, gray for unauthenticated, etc.)

### **Phase 2: Wizard Modal Open (Click LLM button)**
- [ ] Click the LLM button in the header
- [ ] Modal opens with title "LLM Configuration Wizard"
- [ ] **Step 1** displays provider selector (checkboxes for GitHub, OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.)
- [ ] GitHub provider is currently selected (checked)

### **Phase 3: Quick-Model Picker (Step 2)**
- [ ] **Step 2** title appears: "Select Model" or "Quick Models"
- [ ] Quick-pick area shows ~6-8 model buttons arranged horizontally
- [ ] Buttons display model names (e.g., "gemini-flash-latest", "gpt-4-turbo", etc.)
- [ ] At least one recent model appears if you've previously selected one
- [ ] A toggle/link appears labeled "Show Full Catalog" or similar

### **Phase 4: Full Catalog Toggle**
- [ ] Click "Show Full Catalog" toggle
- [ ] Full model table appears below quick-pick area
- [ ] Search input field appears above the table
- [ ] Search input has placeholder text like "Search models..."
- [ ] Click toggle again → table and search input disappear

### **Phase 5: Model Search & Selection**
- [ ] Click "Show Full Catalog" again
- [ ] Type in search field (e.g., "gpt") → table filters to show matching models
- [ ] Clear search → table shows all models again
- [ ] Click a model row in the table (e.g., "gpt-4-turbo")
- [ ] Modal closes
- [ ] Status pill updates to show new provider + model name
- [ ] (If available) Health check badge appears on pill

### **Phase 6: Quick-Model Button Selection**
- [ ] Click LLM button again
- [ ] Select a different provider (e.g., "OpenAI")
- [ ] Quick-pick area updates to show OpenAI models
- [ ] Click one of the quick-pick model buttons
- [ ] Modal closes and status pill updates immediately

### **Phase 7: Recent Model Persistence**
- [ ] Click LLM button again
- [ ] Quick-pick area should show the model you just selected at the top/front
- [ ] Repeat model selections 3+ times across different providers
- [ ] Verify recently-selected models appear in quick-pick order (most recent first)

### **Phase 8: Copilot Auth Panel (Step 3) - Provider Switch**
- [ ] In the modal, locate the provider checkboxes (Step 1)
- [ ] **Select "Copilot/Copilot OAuth"** provider (if available in the list; it should say `copilot-oauth` or similar)
- [ ] Drop down to **Step 3** section
- [ ] Auth panel appears with:
  - Status message (e.g., "Not authenticated" or "Authenticating...")
  - "Start Sign In" button (or similar call-to-action)
  - A section for device code display

### **Phase 9: Copilot Device Flow**
- [ ] Click "Start Sign In" button
- [ ] Device code is generated and displayed (e.g., "ABCD-EFGH")
- [ ] A GitHub authentication URL appears or a note like "Go to: https://github.com/login/device"
- [ ] Status message changes to "Waiting for authorization..." or "Polling..."
- [ ] Poll timeout or cancellation occurs gracefully (no console errors)

### **Phase 10: Model Switching Without Re-wizard**
- [ ] Close the modal (ESC or close button)
- [ ] Wait 2-3 seconds
- [ ] Status pill should remain visible and accurate
- [ ] If you switch tabs/pages, status pill persists
- [ ] Click LLM button again → recent selections are remembered

### **Phase 11: Logout & Auth State Reset (if auth succeeded)**
- [ ] If Copilot auth succeeded, auth panel shows "Log Out" button
- [ ] Click "Log Out"
- [ ] Status on pill changes (e.g., back to "Not authenticated")
- [ ] Auth panel resets to "Start Sign In" state

### **Phase 12: Error Handling & Edge Cases**
- [ ] Search with XSS-like input (e.g., `<script>alert('xss')</script>`) → no alert fired, text escaped cleanly
- [ ] Search with special characters (e.g., `@#$%`) → no crashes, filters gracefully
- [ ] Rapid provider switches → UI updates consistently, no ghost states
- [ ] Close modal while search is active → state resets on next open
- [ ] Network error simulation (stop server briefly) → app shows error message gracefully

---

## How to Use This Checklist

**Run test now in your browser:** Work through each phase in order. For each step, check the box and note any issues or surprising behavior. 

**Report findings back to me** by sharing:
- **Pass/Fail per phase** (number)
- **Any bugs or unexpected behavior** observed
- **Console errors** (press F12 → Console tab, look for red error messages)
- **Browser warnings** (yellow messages in console)

Once you complete the smoke test, I'll either:
- ✅ Confirm all phases passed → prepare commit & PR
- ⚠️ Flag issues found → fix code and re-test
- 🔧 Trace console errors → debug the wizard logic

**Ready?** Start with Phase 1 (app load) and work your way through. Let me know what you find!

 let _pendingPostIntakeContinuation = null;
+
+async function _parseApiJsonResponse(response, endpoint) {
+  const status = Number(response?.status || 0);
+  const statusText = response?.statusText || 'Unknown Status';
+  const contentType = (response?.headers?.get('content-type') || '').toLowerCase();
+  const raw = await response.text();
+
+  if (!response.ok) {
+    let detail = statusText;
+    if (contentType.includes('application/json')) {
+      try {
+        const payload = JSON.parse(raw || '{}');
+        detail = payload?.error || payload?.message || detail;
+      } catch {
+        // Keep fallback detail if malformed JSON error payload.
+      }
+    } else if ((raw || '').trim().startsWith('<')) {
+      detail = 'server returned HTML instead of JSON (possible session redirect or backend error)';
+    } else if ((raw || '').trim()) {
+      detail = raw.trim().slice(0, 220);
+    }
+    throw new Error(`${status}: ${detail}`);
+  }
+
+  if (!contentType.includes('application/json')) {
+    const snippet = (raw || '').trim().slice(0, 80);
+    throw new SyntaxError(
+      `Expected JSON from ${endpoint}, got ${contentType || 'unknown content type'}${snippet ? `: ${snippet}` : ''}`,
+    );
+  }
+
+  try {
+    return parseMessageResponse(JSON.parse(raw || '{}'));
+  } catch (error) {
+    throw new SyntaxError(`Invalid JSON from ${endpoint}: ${error.message}`);
+  }
+}

The provider/model state should be a simple state machine. Example states should include:

_**Agent (copilot/auto)**_

Yes. Your proposed states are the right core set, and I would keep them.

Recommended state set:

1. `Unconfigured`
2. `Configured`
3. `Connecting`
4. `Connected`
5. `Error`
6. `AuthRequired` (add this one)

Why add `AuthRequired`:
- It separates credential problems from generic failures.
- `401/403` should land here, not in generic `Error`.
- This gives clearer UX than “Error” when the fix is specifically sign-in/token.

Optional (only if you want more precision):
1. `RateLimited` for `429`
2. `Unavailable` for provider/network outages (`5xx`, timeouts)

If you want to keep it simple, do not add these optional ones yet. You can still map them to `Error` with different message text.

What I would remove:
- Nothing from your list.
- Do not use “Active/Ready” as independent states unless they map to one of the above.
  - “Ready” should be `Configured` (not yet validated) or `Connected` (validated), never ambiguous.

Suggested transition rules:
- Provider/model chosen successfully -> `Configured`
- Start ping/request -> `Connecting`
- First successful LLM response -> `Connected`
- `401/403` -> `AuthRequired`
- Other failed request -> `Error`
- Config change (provider/model/token) -> back to `Configured` (and clear stale `Connected`)

This gives a clean, deterministic state machine and avoids the “green but not actually connected” issue.

---

_**User (2026-04-02 17:48:13Z)**_

Should there be a 'retry' button for (at least) Error, Rate Limited, and Unavilable?
riately labeled button.

---

_**Agent (copilot/auto)**_

Yes, absolutely.

A Retry button is useful for:
1. Error
2. Rate Limited
3. Unavailable

Recommended behavior by state:
1. Error: show Retry immediately
2. Rate Limited: show Retry with countdown (for example “Retry in 12s”), then enable when timer reaches 0
3. Unavailable: show Retry immediately, optionally with exponential backoff hint after repeated failures

Recommended labels:
1. Error: Retry Request
2. Rate Limited: Retry When Ready (or Retry in Ns while disabled)
3. Unavailable: Reconnect Provider

Recommended UX guardrails:
1. Keep one primary retry action in the chat error card and one in the provider/model panel
2. Prevent duplicate in-flight retries (button disabled while connecting)
3. On click, transition state to Connecting, then to Connected or back to Error/RateLimited/Unavailable
4. Tooltip should explain why retry might fail again (token, quota window, provider outage)

So yes, adding retry is the right move, and it should be state-aware rather than a single generic button.

---

_**User (2026-04-02 17:49:47Z)**_

How should the retry delay be set?   Exponential backoff with a maximum, but allowing the use to adjust?

---

_**Agent (copilot/auto)**_

Yes, that’s the right approach.

Recommended policy:

1. Base algorithm
1. Use exponential backoff with jitter:
   1. $delay_n = \min(cap,\ base \cdot 2^n) + jitter$
   2. Jitter: random 10-25% of delay to avoid synchronized retries.

2. Suggested defaults
1. `base = 1.5s`
2. `cap = 60s`
3. `max_attempts = 6` for automatic retries in one burst

3. Per-state behavior
1. `RateLimited (429)`:
   1. If `Retry-After` header exists, honor it exactly.
   2. Otherwise use exponential schedule with `base=2s`, `cap=90s`.
2. `Unavailable (5xx/timeouts)`:
   1. Use normal exponential schedule (`base=1.5s`, `cap=60s`).
3. `Error`:
   1. One immediate retry allowed, then enter exponential schedule.

4. User adjustment
1. Allow user to adjust:
   1. base delay (for example 1-5s)
   2. max cap (for example 30-180s)
   3. auto-retry on/off
2. Keep defaults safe and apply changes only to future retries (not current countdown).

5. UX behavior
1. Show countdown on button: `Retry in 12s`.
2. Provide “Retry now” override for non-429 states.
3. For 429 with server `Retry-After`, disable “Retry now” until allowed.
4. Tooltip should explain:
   1. current reason
   2. next retry time
   3. whether server-imposed wait is active

6. Safety constraints
1. Reset attempt counter to 0 after any successful request.
2. Reset when provider/model changes.
3. Stop auto-retrying after max attempts and require user action.

If you want, I can implement this with a small retry controller module and wire it to the new `RateLimited` and `Unavailable` states.

_**User (2026-04-02 18:01:20Z)**_

Will the current "Test connection" button capability be preserved ?  If so, how will it interact with the provider/model state machine?

---

_**Agent (copilot/auto)**_

Yes, it should be preserved, and it can become the clean manual trigger for the same state machine.

Recommended interaction model:

1. Keep `Test connection` exactly as a manual probe action.
2. It uses the same state transitions as chat traffic.

Suggested transitions for `Test connection`:
1. On click:
1. `Configured` or `Error/RateLimited/Unavailable` -> `Connecting`
2. On success:
1. `Connecting` -> `Connected`
2. Tooltip: “Provider responded successfully to a live request.”
3. On auth failure (`401/403`):
1. `Connecting` -> `AuthRequired`
2. Tooltip: “Authentication failed. Check API key/token or sign in.”
4. On rate limit (`429`):
1. `Connecting` -> `RateLimited`
2. Tooltip includes retry timing (`Retry-After` if present)
5. On service/network failure (`5xx`, timeout, network):
1. `Connecting` -> `Unavailable` (or `Error` for unknowns)

How it should coexist with auto-connect:
1. Moving into `Configured` can auto-attempt one initial connect.
2. `Test connection` always remains available as:
1. a manual re-check after changing provider/model/settings
2. an override when auto-retry is disabled
3. a direct validation before sending a real prompt

Button behavior details:
1. Disable while currently `Connecting`.
2. Label during probe: `Testing…`
3. Restore label after terminal state.
4. If state is `RateLimited`, show either:
1. disabled with countdown (`Retry in Ns`) when server-imposed wait exists, or
2. enabled manual retry when no strict wait is required.

So short answer: preserve it, wire it to the same state machine, and treat it as the deterministic manual probe path.

function _showModelWizardBusy(message) {
  const overlay = document.getElementById('model-wizard-busy-overlay');
  const messageEl = document.getElementById('model-wizard-busy-message');
  if (messageEl) messageEl.textContent = message || 'Working...';
  if (overlay) overlay.style.display = 'flex';
}

function _hideModelWizardBusy() {
  const overlay = document.getElementById('model-wizard-busy-overlay');
  if (overlay) overlay.style.display = 'none';
}

function _setModelWizardStep(step) {
  _modelWizardStep = [1, 2, 3].includes(step) ? step : 1;
  const providerStep = document.getElementById('model-step-provider');
  const modelStep = document.getElementById('model-step-models');
  const successStep = document.getElementById('model-step-success');
  if (providerStep) providerStep.style.display = _modelWizardStep === 1 ? '' : 'none';
  if (modelStep) modelStep.style.display = _modelWizardStep === 2 ? '' : 'none';
  if (successStep) successStep.style.display = _modelWizardStep === 3 ? '' : 'none';
  _updateModelWizardNav();
}

function _updateModelWizardProgressBar() {
  const steps = [1, 2, 3];
  steps.forEach((stepNum) => {
    const stepEl = document.getElementById(`model-progress-step-${stepNum}`);
    if (!stepEl) return;
    stepEl.classList.remove('is-active', 'is-complete', 'is-upcoming');
    if (stepNum < _modelWizardStep) {
      stepEl.classList.add('is-complete');
    } else if (stepNum === _modelWizardStep) {
      stepEl.classList.add('is-active');
    } else {
      stepEl.classList.add('is-upcoming');
    }
  });
}

function _updateModelWizardNav() {
  const stepLabel = document.getElementById('model-wizard-step-label');
  const backBtn = document.getElementById('model-wizard-back-btn');
  const nextBtn = document.getElementById('model-wizard-next-btn');
  const testBtn = document.getElementById('model-test-btn');
  const refreshBtn = document.getElementById('pricing-refresh-btn');
  const footer = document.querySelector('.model-wizard-footer');

  _updateModelWizardProgressBar();

  if (stepLabel) {
    if (_modelWizardStep === 1) stepLabel.textContent = 'Step 1 of 3: Choose provider';
    if (_modelWizardStep === 2) stepLabel.textContent = 'Step 2 of 3: Choose model and test connection';
    if (_modelWizardStep === 3) stepLabel.textContent = 'Step 3 of 3: Complete';
  }

  if (backBtn) {
    backBtn.disabled = _modelWizardStep === 1;
    backBtn.style.display = _modelWizardStep === 3 ? 'none' : '';
  }
  if (nextBtn) {
    nextBtn.style.display = _modelWizardStep === 1 ? '' : 'none';
    nextBtn.disabled = !_modelWizardSelectedProvider;
  }
  if (testBtn) testBtn.style.display = _modelWizardStep === 2 ? '' : 'none';
  if (refreshBtn) refreshBtn.style.display = _modelWizardStep === 2 ? '' : 'none';
  if (footer) footer.style.justifyContent = _modelWizardStep === 3 ? 'center' : 'space-between';
}

async function _loadModelsForSelectedProvider() {
  if (!_modelWizardSelectedProvider) return false;

  const loadingEl = document.getElementById('model-models-loading');
  if (loadingEl) {
    loadingEl.style.display = '';
    loadingEl.style.color = '#475569';
    loadingEl.innerHTML = '<span class="loading-spinner" style="width:14px;height:14px;border-width:2px;vertical-align:middle;margin-right:6px;"></span>Loading models for selected provider...';
  }

  _showModelWizardBusy('Querying available models...');
  try {
    _selectedModelProviders = new Set([_modelWizardSelectedProvider]);
    _modelData.provider = _modelWizardSelectedProvider;
    await _refreshModelCatalogForSelection();
    await _refreshCopilotAuthPanel();
    if (loadingEl) {
      loadingEl.style.display = 'none';
      loadingEl.textContent = '';
    }
    return true;
  } catch (error) {
    log.warn('Could not load models for selected provider:', error);
    if (loadingEl) {
      loadingEl.style.display = '';
      loadingEl.textContent = 'Failed to load models for selected provider.';
      loadingEl.style.color = '#b91c1c';
    }
    return false;
  } finally {
    _hideModelWizardBusy();
  }
}

async function nextWizardStep() {
  if (_modelWizardStep !== 1) return;
  const loaded = await _loadModelsForSelectedProvider();
  if (!loaded) return;
  _setModelWizardStep(2);
}

function previousWizardStep() {
  if (_modelWizardStep === 2) {
    _setModelWizardStep(1);
    return;
  }
  if (_modelWizardStep === 3) {
    _setModelWizardStep(2);
  }
}

async function openModelModal() {
  const overlay = document.getElementById('model-modal-overlay');
  if (!overlay) return;

  if (!_modelData) {
    await loadModelSelector();
  }
  if (!_modelWizardSelectedProvider) {
    _modelWizardSelectedProvider = _modelData?.provider || null;
  }
  const successSummary = document.getElementById('model-success-summary');
  if (successSummary) {
    successSummary.textContent = 'Provider and model are configured and the connection check succeeded.';
  }
  _renderProviderSelector();
  _syncCatalogVisibility();
  _wireGlobalModelSearch();
  _setModelWizardStep(1);
  _hideModelWizardBusy();
  overlay.style.display = 'flex';
  _focusedElementBeforeModal = document.activeElement;
  setInitialFocus('model-modal-overlay');
  trapFocus('model-modal-overlay');
}

function closeModelModal() {
  const overlay = document.getElementById('model-modal-overlay');
  if (overlay) overlay.style.display = 'none';
  _setModelWizardStep(1);
  _hideModelWizardBusy();
  if (_copilotAuthPollTimer) {
    clearInterval(_copilotAuthPollTimer);
    _copilotAuthPollTimer = null;
  }
  restoreFocus();
}

async function setModel(model, provider) {
  if (!model) return;
  _showModelWizardBusy(`Applying model ${model}...`);
  try {
    const payload = provider ? { model, provider } : { model };
    await apiCall('POST', '/api/model', payload);
    if (_modelData) {
      _modelData.model = model;
      if (provider) _modelData.provider = provider;
    }
    const effectiveProvider = (_modelData && _modelData.provider) || provider;
    const label = document.getElementById('model-current-label');
    if (label) {
      label.textContent = effectiveProvider ? `${effectiveProvider} · ${model}` : model;
    }
    _appendRecentModel(effectiveProvider, model);
    _syncModelTableSelection();
    _renderQuickModelList((_modelData && _modelData.all_models) || []);
    _updateLlmStatusPill('configured', `${effectiveProvider || 'Provider'} configured`);

    _saveModelPrefsToStorage({
      currentModelProvider: effectiveProvider || null,
      currentModelName: model || null,
    });
    await _refreshCopilotAuthPanel();
    await testCurrentModel();
  } catch (e) {
    log.error('Failed to switch model:', e);
    const msg = e.message || String(e);
    _syncModelTableSelection();
    const status = document.getElementById('model-test-status');
    if (status) {
      status.style.display = '';
      status.style.color = '#dc2626';
      status.textContent = `❌ ${msg}`;
    }
    if (typeof appendMessage === 'function') {
      appendMessage('system', `❌ Model switch failed: ${msg}`);
    }
  } finally {
    _hideModelWizardBusy();
  }
}

async function testCurrentModel() {
  // Update both the header badge and the modal status line
  const badge  = document.getElementById('model-test-badge');
  const status = document.getElementById('model-test-status');
  const btn    = document.getElementById('model-test-btn');

  const SPIN = '⏳';
  const OK   = '✅';
  const FAIL = '❌';

  const setRunning = () => {
    if (badge)  { badge.textContent  = SPIN; badge.style.display  = ''; badge.title  = 'Testing…'; }
    if (status) { status.innerHTML   = `${SPIN} Testing connection…`; status.style.display = ''; }
    if (btn)    { btn.disabled = true; btn.textContent = '⏳ Testing…'; }
    _updateLlmStatusPill('connecting', 'Connecting…', '⧗');
  };

  const setOk = (latencyMs) => {
    const tip = `Connected — ${latencyMs}ms`;
    if (badge)  { badge.textContent  = OK;  badge.style.display  = ''; badge.title  = tip; }
    if (status) { status.innerHTML   = `${OK} ${tip}`; status.style.color = '#16a34a'; status.style.display = ''; }
    if (btn)    { btn.disabled = false; btn.innerHTML = '&#10003; Test connection'; }
    _updateLlmStatusPill('connected', `Healthy (${latencyMs}ms)`, '✓');
    const successSummary = document.getElementById('model-success-summary');
    if (successSummary) {
      successSummary.textContent = `Connection verified in ${latencyMs}ms. You can close the wizard and continue.`;
    }
    _setModelWizardStep(3);
  };

  const setFail = (errMsg) => {
    if (badge)  { badge.textContent  = FAIL; badge.style.display  = ''; badge.title  = errMsg; }
    if (status) {
      status.innerHTML   = `${FAIL} <span title="${errMsg.replace(/"/g, '&quot;')}" style="cursor:help; text-decoration:underline dotted;">Connection failed</span>`;
      status.style.color = '#dc2626';
      status.style.display = '';
    }
    if (btn)    { btn.disabled = false; btn.innerHTML = '&#10003; Test connection'; }
    _updateLlmStatusPill('error', 'Connection failed', '⚠', errMsg);
    if (_modelWizardStep === 3) {
      _setModelWizardStep(2);
    }
  };

  setRunning();
  _showModelWizardBusy('Testing model connection...');
  try {
    const result = await apiCall('POST', '/api/model/test');
    if (result.ok) {
      setOk(result.latency_ms);
      return true;
    }
    setFail(result.error || 'Unknown error');
    return false;
  } catch (e) {
    setFail(e.message || String(e));
    return false;
  } finally {
    _hideModelWizardBusy();
  }
}

async function testCurrentModel() {
  // Update both the header badge and the modal status line

  const status = document.getElementById('model-test-status');
  const btn    = document.getElementById('model-test-btn');

  const SPIN = '⏳';
  const OK   = '✅';
  const FAIL = '❌';

  const setRunning = () => {
    if (badge)  { badge.textContent  = SPIN; badge.style.display  = ''; badge.title  = 'Testing…'; }
    if (status) { status.innerHTML   = `${SPIN} Testing connection…`; status.style.display = ''; }
    if (btn)    { btn.disabled = true; btn.textContent = '⏳ Testing…'; }
    _updateLlmStatusPill('connecting', 'Connecting…', '⧗');
  };

  const setOk = (latencyMs) => {
    const tip = `Connected — ${latencyMs}ms`;
    if (badge)  { badge.textContent  = OK;  badge.style.display  = ''; badge.title  = tip; }
    if (status) { status.innerHTML   = `${OK} ${tip}`; status.style.color = '#16a34a'; status.style.display = ''; }
    if (btn)    { btn.disabled = false; btn.innerHTML = '&#10003; Test connection'; }
    _updateLlmStatusPill('connected', `Healthy (${latencyMs}ms)`, '✓');
    setTimeout(() => {
      if (badge  && badge.textContent  === OK)  badge.style.display  = 'none';
      if (status && status.textContent.includes(tip)) status.style.display = 'none';
    }, 30_000);
  };

  const setFail = (errMsg) => {
    if (badge)  { badge.textContent  = FAIL; badge.style.display  = ''; badge.title  = errMsg; }

}

async function refreshModelPricing() {
  const btn = document.getElementById('pricing-refresh-btn');
  const lbl = document.getElementById('pricing-updated-label');
  if (btn) { btn.disabled = true; btn.textContent = 'Refreshing…'; }
  _showModelWizardBusy('Refreshing model pricing...');
  try {
    await apiCall('POST', '/api/model-pricing/refresh');
    // Re-fetch model data so the table gets fresh prices
    _modelData = await apiCall('GET', '/api/model');
    _buildModelTable();
  } catch (e) {
    if (lbl) lbl.textContent = 'Refresh failed';
    log.error('Pricing refresh failed:', e);
  } finally {
    _hideModelWizardBusy();
    if (btn) { btn.disabled = false; btn.textContent = '↻ Refresh prices'; }
  }
}

```
async function startCopilotAuthFromWizard() {
  const statusEl = document.getElementById('model-auth-status');
  const codeEl = document.getElementById('model-auth-code');
  const linkEl = document.getElementById('model-auth-link');
  if (!statusEl || !codeEl || !linkEl) return;

  _showModelWizardBusy('Starting GitHub device authorization...');
  try {
    const flowRes = await fetch('/api/copilot-auth/start', { method: 'POST' });
    if (!flowRes.ok) throw new Error(await flowRes.text());
    const flow = await flowRes.json();

    codeEl.textContent = flow.user_code || '';
    linkEl.href = flow.verification_uri || 'https://github.com/login/device';
    linkEl.style.display = '';
    statusEl.textContent = 'Open GitHub, enter the code, then return here.';
    window.open(linkEl.href, '_blank');

    await fetch('/api/copilot-auth/poll', { method: 'POST' });
    _updateLlmStatusPill('polling', 'Copilot auth pending', '⧗');
    if (_copilotAuthPollTimer) clearInterval(_copilotAuthPollTimer);
    _copilotAuthPollTimer = setInterval(async () => {
      try {
        const st = await fetch('/api/copilot-auth/status').then((res) => res.json());
        if (st.authenticated) {
          clearInterval(_copilotAuthPollTimer);
          _copilotAuthPollTimer = null;
          await _refreshCopilotAuthPanel();
        }
      } catch {
        // keep polling silently until close
      }
    }, 5000);
  } catch (error) {
    statusEl.textContent = `Auth start failed: ${error.message || error}`;
  } finally {
    _hideModelWizardBusy();
  }
}

```

  const statusEl = document.getElementById('model-auth-status');

  const linkEl = document.getElementById('model-auth-link');
  if (!statusEl || !codeEl || !linkEl) return;

  try {
    const flowRes = await fetch('/api/copilot-auth/start', { method: 'POST' });
    if (!flowRes.ok) throw new Error(await flowRes.text());
    const flow = await flowRes.json();

    codeEl.textContent = flow.user_code || '';
    linkEl.href = flow.verification_uri || 'https://github.com/login/device';
    linkEl.style.display = '';
    statusEl.textContent = 'Open GitHub, enter the code, then return here.';
    window.open(linkEl.href, '_blank');

    await fetch('/api/copilot-auth/poll', { method: 'POST' });
    _updateLlmStatusPill('polling', 'Copilot auth pending', '⧗');
    if (_copilotAuthPollTimer) clearInterval(_copilotAuthPollTimer);
    _copilotAuthPollTimer = setInterval(async () => {
      try {

        if (st.authenticated) {
          clearInterval(_copilotAuthPollTimer);
          _copilotAuthPollTimer = null;

  it('toggles full catalog visibility in wizard mode', async () => {
    buildModelFixture()

    const headers = ['Provider', 'Model', 'Context', '$/1M in', '$/1M out', 'Copilot', 'Source', 'Notes']
      .map(text => {
        const th = document.createElement('th')
        th.textContent = text
        return th
      })

    dataTableApi = {
      columns() {
        return {
          every(callback) {
            headers.forEach((_, index) => callback.call({}, index))
          },
        }
      },
      column(index) {
        return {
          header() {
            return headers[index]
          },
          search(value) {
            if (value === undefined) return ''
            return { draw() {} }
          },
        }
      },
      search() {
        return { draw() {} }
      },
    }

    const dollar = vi.fn((selector, attrs) => {
      if (selector instanceof HTMLElement) {
        return makeWrapper(selector)
      }
      if (typeof selector === 'string' && selector.startsWith('<')) {
        const tagMatch = selector.match(/^<([a-z0-9-]+)/i)
        const element = document.createElement(tagMatch[1])
        if (attrs && typeof attrs === 'object') {
          Object.entries(attrs).forEach(([key, value]) => {
            if (key === 'text') {
              element.textContent = value
            } else {
              element.setAttribute(key, value)
            }
          })
        } else {
          const template = document.createElement('template')
          template.innerHTML = selector.trim()
          return makeWrapper(template.content.firstElementChild)
        }
        return makeWrapper(element)
      }
      return makeWrapper(Array.from(document.querySelectorAll(selector)))
    })
    dollar.fn = { DataTable: { isDataTable: vi.fn(() => false) } }

    vi.stubGlobal('$', dollar)
    vi.stubGlobal('fetch', vi.fn().mockResolvedValue({ json: async () => ({ authenticated: false }) }))
    apiCall.mockImplementation(async (_method, url) => {
      if (url === '/api/model') {
        return {
          provider: 'github',
          model: 'gpt-5.4',
          providers: ['github'],
          all_models: [{ provider: 'github', model: 'gpt-5.4', source: 'list_models' }],
          list_models_capable: ['github'],
        }
      }
      if (url.startsWith('/api/model-catalog')) {
        return {
          providers: ['github'],
          all_models: [{ provider: 'github', model: 'gpt-5.4', source: 'list_models' }],
          list_models_capable: ['github'],
        }
      }
      throw new Error(`Unexpected URL: ${url}`)
    })

    await mod.openModelModal()
    await mod.nextWizardStep()
    expect(document.getElementById('model-full-table-wrap').style.display).toBe('none')

    mod.toggleModelCatalogVisibility()
    expect(document.getElementById('model-full-table-wrap').style.display).toBe('')
  })

  it('advances to success pane after a successful connection test', async () => {
    buildModelFixture()

    apiCall.mockImplementation(async (_method, url) => {
      if (url === '/api/model') {

/* -- Stepper -- */
.model-wizard-body { background: #fff; }
.model-wizard-progress {
  display: flex;
  align-items: flex-start;
  padding: 20px 40px 16px;
  border-bottom: 1px solid #e2e8f0;
  background: #f8fafc;
}
.model-progress-step {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  align-items: center;
  gap: 8px;
  min-width: 72px;
}
.model-progress-badge {
  width: 32px;
  height: 32px;
  border-radius: 50%;
  display: inline-flex;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: center;
  font-size: 13px;
  font-weight: 700;
  border: 2px solid transparent;
  transition: background 0.25s ease, box-shadow 0.25s ease, color 0.25s ease;
}
.model-progress-text {
  font-size: 11px;
  font-weight: 600;
  text-align: center;
  white-space: nowrap;
  letter-spacing: 0.01em;
  transition: color 0.25s ease;
}
.model-progress-connector {
  flex: 1;
  height: 2px;
  background: #e2e8f0;
  margin-top: 15px;
  border-radius: 999px;
  min-width: 32px;
  transition: background 0.3s ease;
}
.model-progress-connector.is-complete { background: #16a34a; }
/* Active step */
.model-progress-step.is-active .model-progress-badge {
  background: #2563eb;
  color: #fff;
  border-color: #2563eb;
  box-shadow: 0 0 0 4px #dbeafe;
}
.model-progress-step.is-active .model-progress-text { color: #1e40af; font-weight: 700; }
/* Completed step */
.model-progress-step.is-complete .model-progress-badge {
  background: #16a34a;
  color: #fff;
  border-color: #16a34a;
}
.model-progress-step.is-complete .model-progress-text { color: #15803d; }
/* Upcoming step */
.model-progress-step.is-upcoming .model-progress-badge {
  background: #fff;
  color: #94a3b8;
  border-color: #cbd5e1;
}
.model-progress-step.is-upcoming .model-progress-text { color: #94a3b8; }
/* -- Step pane content -- */
.model-wizard-pane { min-height: 320px; }
.model-wizard-step-section {
  padding: 16px 20px;
  border-bottom: 1px solid #e2e8f0;
  background: #f8fafc;
}
.model-wizard-step-header {
  font-size: 0.875em;
  font-weight: 600;
  color: #334155;
  margin-bottom: 10px;
}
.model-wizard-step-hint {
  margin-top: 10px;
  font-size: 0.82em;
  color: #64748b;
  line-height: 1.5;
}
/* -- Success pane -- */
.model-wizard-success {
  min-height: 320px;
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: center;
  gap: 12px;
  text-align: center;
  padding: 28px 24px;
}
.model-wizard-success-icon {
  width: 64px;
  height: 64px;
  border-radius: 999px;
  background: #16a34a;
  color: #fff;
  display: inline-flex;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: center;
  font-size: 32px;
  font-weight: 700;
  box-shadow: 0 10px 24px rgba(22, 163, 74, 0.24);
}
.model-wizard-success h3 { color: #14532d; font-size: 24px; }
.model-wizard-success p { max-width: 520px; color: #166534; font-size: 14px; line-height: 1.55; }
.model-wizard-primary-close {
  margin-top: 8px;
  border: none;
  border-radius: 10px;
  padding: 12px 26px;
  font-size: 15px;
  font-weight: 700;
  background: #16a34a;
  color: #fff;
  cursor: pointer;
  box-shadow: 0 6px 16px rgba(22, 163, 74, 0.24);
}
.model-wizard-primary-close:hover { background: #15803d; }
/* -- Busy overlay -- */
.wizard-busy-overlay {
  position: absolute;
  inset: 0;
  z-index: 12;
  display: none;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: center;
  background: rgba(15, 23, 42, 0.42);
  backdrop-filter: blur(1px);
}
.wizard-busy-card {
  min-width: 320px;
  max-width: 88%;
  padding: 22px 24px;
  border-radius: 14px;
  border: 1px solid rgba(148, 163, 184, 0.45);
  background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.98);
  box-shadow: 0 20px 30px rgba(15, 23, 42, 0.2);
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: 14px;
}
.wizard-busy-spinner { width: 28px; height: 28px; border-width: 3px; }
.wizard-busy-message { color: #0f172a; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 600; }
/* -- Wizard footer -- */
.model-wizard-footer {
  justify-content: space-between;
  align-items: center;
  flex-wrap: wrap;
  gap: 8px;
  font-size: 0.85em;
  color: #64748b;
  background: #f8fafc;
  padding: 10px 16px;
}
.model-wizard-footer-meta {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: 10px;
  color: #64748b;
  font-size: 0.85em;
}
.model-wizard-footer-actions {
  display: flex;
  gap: 6px;
  align-items: center;
}
